Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT February 10, 2006 MAYOR VICENTE P. EUSEBIO Pasig City Dear Mayor Eusebio: This refers to your request for this Department's legal opinion involving the succession of barangay elective officials. Per your letter, the following facts are presented, to wit: • The Punong Barangay of Barangay Bambang, that City was elected as City Councilor, thus, a permanent vacancy in the said position occurred; On account thereof, the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay Member, pursuant to Section 44 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), became the Punong Barangay; • However, this successor — Punong Barangay was placed under preventive suspension by the Ombudsman. You are now in a quandary as to who shall be the "legal successor" to the Office of the Punong Barangay, as it is your view that Section 44 (b) of RA 7160 applies only once, which means that when the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member has assumed the position of Punong Barangay, the rule on automatic succession is no longer applicable and also, the rule on automatic succession only applies to the position of a duly elected Punong Barangay and not to the official who succeeded. Hence, your query. In reply thereto, please be informed that the rule of permanent succession under Section 44 (b) of RA 7160 is not singly applied. Everytime the post of Punong Barangay becomes permanently vacant, the highest sangguniang barangay member shall become the Punong Barangay by operation of law. The only time succession stops is when there is nobody to succeed anymore from the regular members of the sangguniang barangay. The SK Chairman, as ex-officio member of the

-2- Sangguniang Barangay, cannot succeed because ex-officio members in all sanggunians do not have ranks and therefore, have no successional rights. On the proposition that the rule of succession applies only to the position of a duly elected Punong Barangay and not to the official who assumed the said office by succession, we find this to be legally untenable. It is well to note that while the LGC provides that Punong Barnagays are chosen by way of election, the same Code, however, particularly Section 44 (b) thereof, provides for the legal procedure under which a permanent vacancy in the Punong Barangay position shall be filled up. In either mode, the occupant of the Punong Barangay position is considered the legal holder thereof such that if a permanent or temporary vacancy occurs in the same position, the law pertaining to the filling up of said vacancy shall now find application, and none other. In the case at bar, please note that the preventive suspension of the "successor" — Punong Barangay gave rise to a temporary, not permanent vacancy in the Office of the Punong Barangay. Ergo, the applicable provision in this case is Section 46 (a) of RA 7160 re: temporary vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive, and not Section 44 (b) thereof. When the successor - Punong Barangay becomes temporarily incapacitated to perform the duties and responsibilities of said office, the 1st ranking Sangguniang Barangay Member (who was originally the 2nd ranking Sangguniang Barangay Member), by operation of law, shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local Chief Executive in an acting capacity until the temporary incapacity of the Punong Barangay subsists, subject to the limitations provided under Section 46 (a) of the Code. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Leg*7/cga cc ; Bir. Rodolfo DILG-NCR Very truly yours, TERESITA S. CASTILLO Undersecretar S - Ferax-en
